### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. PCWH syndrome  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.787)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:11190)

**Proposed mechanism:** SOX10 (HGNC:11190) —DISRUPTS→ Sox10 transcriptional regulation network (REACT:R-HSA-113804); Sox10 transcriptional regulation network (REACT:R-HSA-113804) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); Sox10 transcriptional regulation network (REACT:R-HSA-113804) —LEADS_TO→ Hypoplastic or absent corpus callosum (HP:0001274); Sox10 transcriptional regulation network (REACT:R-HSA-113804) —LEADS_TO→ Hypopigmentation of the skin (HP:0001004); Sox10 transcriptional regulation network (REACT:R-HSA-113804) —LEADS_TO→ Sensorineural hearing impairment (HP:0000405). Haploinsufficiency of SOX10 disrupts its transcriptional regulatory network, leading to a range of developmental defects including intellectual disability, hypoplastic or absent corpus callosum, hypopigmentation, and sensorineural hearing impairment, which are common to both MONDO:0012698 and PCWH syndrome (MONDO:0012198).

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in SOX10 that are consistently associated with only one of the two diseases, or the absence of SOX10 variants in individuals diagnosed with one of the diseases, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: rs756484176)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of SOX10 in these disorders could enable the development of therapeutic strategies targeting common downstream pathways, potentially benefiting patients with either condition.

#### 2. Waardenburg syndrome type 4C  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.786)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:11190)

**Proposed mechanism:** SOX10 (HGNC:11190) —DISRUPTS→ Neural crest cell development and migration (GO:0001707); Neural crest cell development and migration (GO:0001707) —LEADS_TO→ Hirschsprung disease (MONDO:0012698); Neural crest cell development and migration (GO:0001707) —LEADS_TO→ Waardenburg syndrome type 4C (MONDO:0013202); Neural crest cell development and migration (GO:0001707) —LEADS_TO→ Pigmentation defects (HP:0001007); Neural crest cell development and migration (GO:0001707) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital deafness (HP:0000365). **How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in SOX10 that are associated with gain-of-function or dominant-negative effects, rather than haploinsufficiency, in patients with these specific phenotypes would falsify this hypothesis.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism involving SOX10 in neural crest development offers a potential therapeutic target for both congenital enteric nervous system disorders and pigmentation/auditory deficits, possibly through gene therapy or small molecule modulators aimed at restoring SOX10 function or compensating for its loss.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of a pathogenic variant in PMP22 or MPZ with a significantly high allele frequency (>0.1%) in gnomAD for the specific population affected by the respective disease, or demonstration of distinct molecular pathways affected by mutations in PMP22 versus MPZ that do not converge on myelin integrity. _(variant: rs121918220)_
